claim_register.claim: The dated requirement limits split functionality to FMRP flows. It excludes BCS/LOANIQ and historical Razor-routed EG/NP/SA, with EG/NP/SA inclusion conditional on strategic migration before go-live. Manual split requires New, WAITING or READY, no netting ID, no splitting ID and non-LOANIQ source. PROJECTED eligibility is struck through. The action profile matches netting; no manual split rule is required. Manual splitting of generic and IRS netting resultants has conflicting dated scope and test rows. No current resultant permission is selected.

claim_register.claim: Preview starts with the original amount. Reducing an amount creates another child for the balance. Each input must be greater than zero and below available balance, using currency rounding precision. SI lookup is optional and uses the adhoc-SSI profile. Split With Affirmation requests affirmation details and marks children affirmed, without Pending Affirmation. One user approves the split action; child release still follows its exception controls. The parent becomes SPLIT. Children use an S prefix and length12, return to the main workflow and wait with Split Cashflow. Splitting_Id links parent and children and supports queries/display. No populated sample identity is retained.

claim_register.claim: Amendment requires at least two WAITING children. Only their amounts can change; users cannot add/delete children. Preserve the original total after excluding ineligible-child amounts from the available balance. The source records no authorization-limit restriction for the split action, and one-user amendment without checker. Children retain Split Cashflow plus Split Amend; parent remains SPLIT. Unsplit requires a splitting ID, New event and no RELEASED/SETTLED child. Its main list permits QUEUED,WAITING,FAILED,HOLD,READY with NA, CASHFLOW_SUPPRESSED and SWIFT_SUPPRESSED. The demo omits SWIFT_SUPPRESSED, leaving applicability unresolved. Success makes children DEAD and returns parent to WAITING with Un-Split. The demo removes splitting ID.

claim_register.claim: SPLIT and unsplit changes write back to Stella, not Murex. A released child, or a child settled without prior release, writes back to Murex where applicable, including underlying net components. Split children cannot manually split, net, hit automatic/NDS netting rules or run IRS checks; automatic splitting remains allowed. SPLIT generates no accounting and cannot move to FAILED. Trade Undo after SPLIT moves the new event to ERROR. Non-economic withdrawal/new is ignored when SPLIT has a released/settled child, or manual touch exists; untouched flows process the latest version. Blade hard-blocks split status; Stella and DQSL require split state/field support.

claim_register.claim: The main rule splits parent withdrawal into child withdrawals: unreleased children CANCELLED; released-child withdrawal waits for manual action, and withdrawal parent remains SPLIT. A later test expects unreleased-child withdrawal to auto-unsplit, make children DEAD and cancel parent. The net-component test additionally auto-unnets, cancels the withdrawn component, returns its partner WAITING and makes resultant/children DEAD. Released-child tests hold withdrawal NSTP and then expect READY with Swift error after manual release. Dated IRS notes disagree about reversal accounting and manual-split permission. These are unresolved expected outcomes, not observed execution.

claim_register.claim: DataOps maintains Nostro Threshold Static with maker/checker; other users read only. Currency, threshold, amount and limitation are mandatory. Entity and Nostro-agent BIC are optional; missing entity produces a warning. Agent BIC length is8/11. Numeric fields have no decimals; amount is below threshold and limitation, and limitation below threshold. Duplicate key is entity+agent+currency. The main design uses create/update/disable, while the demo lists delete. Confirm the effective action contract. Before Swift generation, pay cashflows meeting static with amount>=threshold automatically split. Best-match order is currency, entity, then Nostro agent. Net resultants and existing split children may auto-split. Each child generates its own Swift/accounting. Exact selected threshold records still require owner confirmation.

claim_register.claim: The algorithm proposes accumulated deductions below threshold, skipping every tenth child, separating duplicate final amounts and reducing deduction by ten when limits are reached. The selected text is incomplete without its images. A deduction below one raises an exception to stop infinite splitting. The first design uses AutoSplitFail into READY/NA/PendingException. A later proposal replaces that action with TechFail and a comment because withdrawal handling from that state is source-reported as unsupported. Actual TechFail result/comment details remain in an uninspected image. Split Cashflow, Split Amend, Un-Split and Withdrawal on Split rules each use MAKER_CHECKER,NSTP and no bulk eligibility.
